title: Hype Meter Sorter
description: A claim-sorting game. Sixteen real gut-brain claims from across the book appear one at a time; the learner grades each as Strong, Moderate, Preliminary, or Hype, then sees the book's grade and a one-sentence evidence reason. A running tally shows matches and whether misses were too generous or too harsh.
creator: Aaryav Sharma
subject: neuroscience (gut-brain axis)
publisher: Gut Check: The Neuroscience of How Your Gut and Brain Talk
learningObjectives: Evaluate popular gut-brain claims by assigning a Hype Meter grade (Strong, Moderate, Preliminary, or Hype) based on the kind and amount of evidence behind each claim as stated.
Judge whether one's own grading tends to be too generous or too harsh, and explain which evidence features (mouse or human, study size, correlation or cause) drive a grade.
prerequisites: The four Hype Meter grades and the six claim questions (Chapter 1)
Basic idea of a randomized controlled trial
keyQuestions: Was the claim tested in people or only in mice?
Does the evidence show cause or only a link?
How many people were studied, and do several studies agree?
Why can a claim built on a true fact still earn a Hype grade?
misconceptions: If a claim mentions a real study, it must be Strong.
Everything about the gut-brain axis is hype, so every claim deserves a low grade.
An FDA approval for one condition means the treatment works for other conditions.
A true number (such as 70% of plasma cells) supports a bigger claim (70% of the immune system).
